newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Horn says looking to settle dam row with Slovakia.
newsitem.headline: Horn says looking to settle dam row with Slovakia.

text.p: Hungarian prime minister Gyula Horn confirmed on Tuesday that Hungary and Slovakia were exploring an out-of-court settlement to their dispute over Slovakia's decision to divert Danube waters in a dam project.
"The Slovak attitude has changed," Horn told reporters on Tuesday. "There is now an attitude to the negotiation that we should try to reach an agreement -- this is a very constructive standpoint."
Meciar and Horn met on Monday after a trilateral meeting with Austria in the west Slovak spa town of Piestany.

The countries are in dispute over Slovakia's unilateral decision to divert waters of the Danube for its Gabcikovo hydro-electric dam project after Hungary in 1989 quit a joint project for a similar dam downstream at Nagymaros in Hungary. @
Slovakia claims Hungary broke its contract while the Hungarians say diverting the water breaches international law and has caused environmental damage to a marsh region in northwestern Hungary.
They had agreed to take the case to the World Court in the Hague, which is due to consider it early next year.
A spokeswoman for Meciar told journalists after Monday's meeting that both sides saw room for settlement of the dispute.

Horn said on Tuesday a committee would be set up to explore an out-of-court deal. The committee's make-up would be finalised by the two countries' foreign ministers at a Central European Initiative summit in Graz, Austria, this weekend.
"There is no guarantee that agreement can be reached but, in matters which are taken to the Hague, the court looks favourably on the fact that two parties try to reach agreement" Horn said.
